name: Congenital muscular alpha-dystroglycanopathy with brain and eye anomalies
aliases: Alpha-dystroglycanopathy congenital form with brain and ocular involvement
Congenital muscular dystrophy with alpha-dystroglycan deficiency and brain-eye anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for congenital muscular alpha-dystroglycanopathy with brain and eye anomalies

criteria.description: Congenital hypotonia and muscle weakness with delayed motor milestones
Neuroimaging evidence of brain anomalies such as cobblestone lissencephaly or cerebellar hypoplasia
Presence of structural eye abnormalities including retinal dysplasia or optic nerve hypoplasia
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes affecting alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation (e.g., POMT1, POMT2, FKRP)
Muscle biopsy showing reduced or absent alpha-dystroglycan immunoreactivity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital hypotonia and muscle weakness plus neuroimaging-confirmed brain anomalies and ocular abnormalities, supported by genetic confirmation of alpha-dystroglycanopathy-related mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology, ophthalmology, neuroimaging, and genetic testing.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital hypotonia with profound muscle weakness
searchTerms: low muscle tone and severe weakness from birth
profound muscle weakness present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cobblestone lissencephaly detected on brain MRI
searchTerms: brain surface looks bumpy and smooth on MRI
abnormal brain surface with cobblestone appearance

pathognomonic.symptomName: Retinal dysplasia and optic nerve hypoplasia
searchTerms: abnormal retina and small optic nerve
retinal malformation with optic nerve underdevelopment
eye abnormalities affecting retina and optic nerve

common.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones including inability to sit or walk independently
searchTerms: unable to sit or walk independently on time
involuntary eye movements and crossed eyes

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to oropharyngeal muscle weakness
searchTerms: difficulty feeding due to weak throat muscles
feeding issues from muscle weakness in mouth

common.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency secondary to muscle weakness
searchTerms: respiratory failure due to muscle weakness
epileptic fits related to cortical abnormalities
brain seizure activity from structural defects

occasional.symptomName: Visual impairment due to retinal involvement
searchTerms: poor eyesight due to retinal damage

occasional.symptomName: Hypotonic facial muscles causing poor facial expression
searchTerms: weak facial muscles causing poor expressions
fluid buildup in brain needing shunting

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate elevation)
Muscle biopsy showing reduced alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation
imaging: Brain MRI demonstrating cobblestone lissencephaly, cerebellar hypoplasia, and white matter abnormalities
Ocular imaging revealing retinal dysplasia and optic nerve hypoplasia
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation (e.g., POMT1, POMT2, FKRP, FKTN)
other: Ophthalmologic examination confirming structural eye anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: More severe brain malformations including hydrocephalus
Similar ocular anomalies but often more profound
Milder brain malformations compared to congenital muscular alpha-dystroglycanopathy
Characteristic brain MRI findings with polymicrogyria
Distinct genetic mutations in FKTN gene

redFlags: Severe congenital hypotonia with respiratory failure
Progressive visual impairment with structural eye anomalies
Neuroimaging revealing cobblestone lissencephaly or cerebellar hypoplasia
